title: Porsche PCCM Plus yeni ekranları eski modellerle buluşturuyor
summary: Porsche, 2009-2016 yılları arasındaki eski Boxster, Cayman ve 911 modelleri için Apple CarPlay ve Android Auto destekli yeni multimedya sistemlerini duyurdu.
body:
Porsche PCCM Plus yeni ekranları eski modellerle buluşturuyor ve sürücülere modern bağlantı seçenekleri sunuyor. Carscoops'un aktardığına göre Alman otomobil üreticisi, 2009 ile 2016 yılları arasında üretilen eski nesil araçlar için geliştirilen iki yeni multimedya sistemi tanıttı.

## Yeni sistemler neler sunuyor?

Yeni cihazlar 2009-2016 model yıllarını kapsayan Boxster, Cayman ve 911 serisi araçların konsollarına tam uyum sağlayacak şekilde tasarlandı. Her iki ünitede de 7 inçlik dokunmatik ekran yer alırken, sürücüler direksiyon üzerindeki kontrolleri de kullanabiliyor.

Sistemler Apple CarPlay ve Android Auto desteğinin yanı sıra Bluetooth, Wi-Fi ve 4G veri erişimi sunuyor. Harita güncellemeleri kablosuz olarak yapılırken, kullanıcılar araç durur haldekideyken YouTube videolarını izleyebiliyor ve ekran üzerindeki sanal aracın rengini gerçek otomobillerine göre değiştirebiliyor. Cihazların ABD'deki Porsche bayilerine önümüzdeki yılın başlarında gelmesi beklenirken, fiyat bilgisi henüz paylaşılmadı.

**Neden önemli?** Eski lüks otomobiller mekanik olarak güçlü kalsa da bilgi-eğlence teknolojileri açısından hızla eskidiği için, bu tür yükseltmeler eski model araç sahiplerinin modern sürüş kolaylıklarına kavuşmasını sağlıyor.

source_texts.title: Porsche Just Vanished Another Reason Not To Daily A Used Cayman Or 911
source_texts.summary: Infotainment retrofit option has been expanded to bring CarPlay and Android Auto to multiple Porsche models built between 2009-16
source_texts.text:
- Porsche has released two new upgraded media systems for its older cars.
- The two double-DIN units work with the 2009-16 Boxster, Cayman and 911.
- Both feature a 7-inch touchscreen and Android Auto and Apple CarPlay.
The biggest telltale of car’s age isn’t its power, performance or handling. It’s the infotainment and connectivity. Even cars that cost big bucks 10 or 15 years ago can feel ancient once you start dealing with period media and navigation systems. But Porsche has a fix that gives owners of older models all the connivence of newer ones, while looking like they’ve never been messed with.
Porsche’s Classic Communication Management Plus (PCCM Plus) systems aren’t new. They’ve been around since 2020, and to date more than 300,000 units have been sold to owners of 996-generation 911s and first-generation 986 and 987.1 Boxsters and Caymans. Even old air cooled 911s are covered by a single-DIN PCCM kit. But now the brand is expanding availability to the next wave of neo-classic Porsches from 2009 to 2016.
Related: Volkswagen Turns Your Parked Car Into A Game Console For $149 A Year
The two new PCCM Plus infotainment units are designed to slot into the consoles of the 981.2, 981, 997.2 and 991.1. Which, in case you don’t speak Porsche geek, means they’ll fit the 2009-12 and 2013-16 Boxter and Cayman, and 2009-13 and 2012-16 911.
Most, but not all, of those cars, came with a touchscreen media unit from the factory, and the new systems are designed to fit seamlessly into the stock dashboard aperture. Each gets a 7-inch touchscreen, though drivers can also control functions using the stock steering wheel controls, where fitted. So not you, GT3 owners.
Navigation instructions and music tracks can be displayed in the instrument cluster, and you get all of the convenience kit you expect from a modern car, including Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, Bluetooth for phone calls and Wi-Fi. Speed limits are also shown to help stop you getting carried away, and Boxster and Cayman models get visual parking assistance instead of just audio guidance.
YouTube, But Not On The Move
European systems come with DAB radio, the US gets HD, and all units have FM and AM tuners, plus Bluetooth streaming. You can even watch YouTube videos when stationary (if your country allows it) and change the color of the virtual car on the screen to match your car’s real exterior color.
Navigation maps can be viewed as satellite images, and a Scenic Roads nav function will send you by the most fun route instead of just the quickest. A nano SIM gives 4G data access and map revisions are handled by over-the-air updates, so there’s no need to trek down to your Porsche dealer, or drag your laptop into the garage every year.
Porsche hasn’t revealed prices for the two new systems yet, but if you go with the automaker’s recommendation to let an official service center fit one to your car, we imagine you won’t get much change from $3k. We’ll find out early next year when the units hit US Porsche dealers.
